https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/a.text: There are dozens of Australians missing in Nepal including (clockwise from left): Karan Bhardwaj, Chitra Venkatraman, Venkatraman Balakrishnan, Sumi Adhikari and Shylaja, Aarush, Ashwin and Chandrasekaran Muralitharan Composite: Supplied by the families View image in fullscreen There are dozens of Australians missing in Nepal including (clockwise from left): Karan Bhardwaj, Chitra Venkatraman, Venkatraman Balakrishnan, Sumi Adhikari and Shylaja, Aarush, Ashwin and Chandrasekaran Muralitharan Composite: Supplied by the families Nepal-Tibet flood disaster ‘So desperately loved’: ADF member among dozens of Australians missing in Nepal floods as families pray for safe return Relatives ‘really worried, but hopeful’ as they wait anxiously for news in the aftermath of the flash flooding disaster Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Henry Belot , Nino Bucci and Kat Wong Fri 28 Aug 2026 05.52 EDT First published on Thu 27 Aug 2026 22.19 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The families of an Australian defence force member and two Sydney boys who went missing with their parents in Nepal remain hopeful they will be found safe. Dozens of Australians are missing after devastating flooding on the Nepal-Tibet border. Nepal’s disaster management authority said on Friday that the total number of people missing had risen sharply to more than 1,900 swelled by 933 workers on hydropower projects on the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli rivers where a wall of water powered down on Wednesday morning. The number of people killed is at least 579. One Australian woman contacted her family on Friday morning to tell them that she had survived the flood, the first of those reported missing to be confirmed safe. Among the missing Australians is Karan Bhardwaj, a 40-year-old Brisbane-based member of the Royal Australian air force who was travelling in Nepal with Kailash Journeys. “Karan is a dad to my beautiful seven-year-old nephew, as well as a brother, uncle and brother in law,” said his family member Jen, who did not want her surname published. Race to get aid into Nepal and Tibet amid warnings flood lake could burst Read more “He is so desperately loved by his family and right now we are desperately praying, hoping and believing that Karan is safe, alive and somehow making his way back to us.” Shylaja Muralitharan, 42, her husband, Chandrasekaran Muralitharan, 47, and their two sons Ashwin, 14, and Aarush, 11, were taking part in a pilgrimage when the flood hit on Wednesday. Shylaja’s younger sister, Vaishnavi, said that she had lost contact with the family shortly after breakfast on the morning of the flood. 2:02 Timeline of how deadly Nepal and Tibet flash flood unfolded – explainer The family of four planned to head towards an immigration checkpoint on the Tibet-Nepal border soon after, as part of the group of 15 Australians trekking with the Himalayan Glacier Adventures tour. “Just like everyone else that’s part of that group, we’re really worried, but hopeful,” Vaishnavi said. “Hopeful that they’re safe and just waiting to be rescued. “It’s a very difficult time for our whole family … I just want to make people aware that they’re there, and we’re waiting, and we just want them to return.” Vaishnavi, who asked that her surname not be published, confirmed the family were close with other members of the group who had also travelled from Sydney for the Hindu pilgrimage to Mount Kailash in Tibet. Sign up for the Breaking News Australia email The family had been training together for the long walk, she said. “They had been planning for some time, and preparing, because it’s quite a trek. “They were all working very hard together to make sure they could successfully complete it. “We just didn’t expect anything like this.” A map of the flood affected areas Vaishnavi said it was difficult to get clear information about what was being done to find those missing. She has spoken with Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade officials. “We do want to know what efforts are being made … we’re not aware of what is actually happening there.” Australian woman Sumi Adhikari was at an immigration office at the Gyirong Post crossing when the flood waters hit. She was travelling with an Isha Foundation pilgrimage to the region. Her husband, Nava Pandey, has travelled to Nepal and is desperately seeking information about her whereabouts. “She was in the same area when the flood happened,” said a flyer produced by Adhikari’s family, and published with their permission. “If anyone has seen her or has any information about her, please contact the family immediately.” View image in fullscreen Sumi Adhikari was travelling as part of an Isha Foundation pilgrimage. Illustration: supplied Bharat Mangwani, 42, was travelling with the Isha Foundation as part of a pilgrimage to Lake Manasarovar when his family lost contact with him on Wednesday morning. He was last seen at Gyirong before the group was set to depart for Kathmandu and then Delhi, his close friend Kushagra Tiwari said. Mangwani’s family, including his nine-year-old son and three-year-old daughter, have travelled to India with a family friend, while his wife has gone on to Kathmandu to look for any information. “All of us are praying for him and hopefully he comes back to us soon,” Tiwari said. Suhasini Kandimalla, a mother of two from Springfield, near Brisbane, has also been reported missing. Her sister, Supreethini Kandimalla, said that she was doing the hike with another Springfield local. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | When needed Sign up to Breaking News Australia Get the most important news as it breaks after newsletter promotion Suhasini Kandimalla from Queensland who has been reported missing in Nepal. Photograph: Supplied While she was a New Zealand citizen, Suhasini had been approved for Australian citizenship, her sister said. She had planned to attend a citizenship ceremony for it to be granted soon after she returned. “I don’t know if it was a religious calling for her to do it,” Supreethini told the Guardian. “But she certainly loved the treks in New Zealand too, and would go on lots of long hikes.” A Brisbane man, Narayan Panthi, is also missing in the region. According to Nepal police, he was travelling with Kathmandu Holiday but he has also been conducting charity work in the capital with an education fund, the NeNas Foundation. View image in fullscreen Narayan Panthi from Brisbane is missing in Nepal. Photograph: Supplied Panthi’s cousin, Amrit Bhusal, said his family was devastated but “holding on to hope and praying for positive news”. “We are still hoping,” Bhusal said. “We are still searching. We are still praying for Narayan to come home safely.” Bhusal said Panthi was “helping disadvantaged children in Nepal reach their full potential through education”. New South Wales couple Venkatraman Balakrishnan, 52, and his wife, Chitra Venkatraman, 46, were also among the 15 Australians travelling to Mount Kailash. So too were Sreedharan and Lakshmi Iyer, and their adult sons Rishab, 23, and Rudhra, 20. The brothers played cricket for West Pennant Hills Cherrybrook Cricket Club in Sydney’s north-west. “WPHCCC is aware of the reports that two of our players, Rishab and Rudhra Iyer, along with their family members and other Australians, are unaccounted for in the ongoing floods in Nepal,” the club said in a statement. What caused the catastrophic flood in Nepal and Tibet – and how does a glacier collapse? Read more “We continue to live in hope, and our thoughts are currently with them, their loved ones and all affected by this tragedy in Nepal.” The University of Newcastle’s vice-chancellor, Alex Zelinsky, said Rishab and Rudhra were both medical students the at the university. “We are thinking of them, their families, their fellow students and teaching staff, as well as the many people who have been impacted by this devastating event and we hope that both students can be located soon,” Zelinsky said in a statement. Separate groups of Australians – 11 travelling with Trekkers Society and six with Kailash Journeys – are also unaccounted for. Both tour companies have been contacted for comment. Several other Australians were travelling with other tour groups. It is understood the majority of missing Australians are from New South Wales, but there are also some from Victoria and Queensland. The founder and chief executive of Himalayan Glacier Adventures, Sagar Pandey, said he had lost all contact with his tour group of 47 people, which included the 15 Australians. Pandey told the Guardian on Thursday he had flown by helicopter over the Rasuwa area, where the tour was staying, since the flood and had little hope they survived. “To be honest … you would think there was no human civilisation there at all. “The flash flood swept away everything, everything. You couldn’t see any human creations. “Still, I have a hope.” The Isha Foundation confirmed that 11 Australians were among a group of 80 missing pilgrims who had been in an immigration building when the flood hit. The foreign minister, Penny Wong, spoke to her Nepali counterpart, Shisir Khanal, on Friday evening to convey Australia’s deepest condolences following the devastating floods. She outlined Australia’s humanitarian assistance package in which Australia was “rapidly mobilising consular and humanitarian support in response” to the flooding. Wong said the government would send an initial team of three humanitarian response specialists “within the next 48 hours’” to help Australian staff already on the ground. “The extraordinary scale of this disaster and the remoteness of the affected region mean immense challenges lie ahead for the response and recovery.” Explore more on these topics Nepal-Tibet flood disaster news Share Reuse this content More on this story More on this story Pauline Hanson courts wealthy donors with $2,000 ‘exclusive’ Melbourne lunch, but where are the receipts? https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2026.text: British Transport Police funding cuts ‘have been disastrous’, said the general secretary of the RMT union, Eddie Dempsey. Photograph: Murdo MacLeod/The Guardian View image in fullscreen British Transport Police funding cuts ‘have been disastrous’, said the general secretary of the RMT union, Eddie Dempsey. Photograph: Murdo MacLeod/The Guardian Rail transport Reported assaults on Great Britain’s railways rise by fifth in a year Unions say record high of nearly 25,000, including assaults on rail workers and public, shows need for more staff and policing Gwyn Topham Transport correspondent Thu 24 Sep 2026 12.00 EDT First published on Thu 24 Sep 2026 08.20 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The number of reported assaults on Great Britain’s railways has risen by a fifth to a record high of almost 25,000 incidents in a year. Unions said the “horrendous” figures showed the need for more staff and policing, as the Office of Rail and Road (ORR) revealed a sharp increase in assaults on the travelling public and on railway staff last year. There were 13,464 reported assaults against passengers and members of the public on the mainline railway in 2025-26, up 36% on the previous year and the highest number recorded by the ORR since it started tracking the figures in 2004. Assaults on rail staff were up 12% in a year to 11,289 reported incidents, mainly verbal abuse but including nearly 2,500 physical assaults – an average of about seven every day. The assaults on members of the public included startling rises in cases of harassment, up 52% year on year, and common assault, up by 30%. The figures partly reflect increased reporting and zero-tolerance campaigns on public transport, but also underline concerns flagged by unions about the threats to frontline workers as well as passengers, and the availability of transport police . The RMT general secretary, Eddie Dempsey, said the numbers were horrendous but chimed with the union’s own surveys showing two-thirds of its members had experienced some form of violence at work in the past year. He said: “We are calling for a significant increase in staffing across public transport, including an end to lone working. We also clearly need stronger legal protections for public transport workers against assaults at work. “British Transport Police funding cuts have also been disastrous which has undermined a proper policing presence on all public transport.” The TSSA union’s general secretary, Maryam Eslamdoust, said: “These new figures are shocking but not surprising because we have been warning for many months that violence on the railways is spiralling out of control.” The government said it was increasing police funding and taking the issue “extremely seriously”. A Department for Transport spokesperson said: “The rise in assaults on the railway is deeply concerning and completely unacceptable. No passenger or rail worker should face violence, threats or abuse, and we encourage anyone affected to report incidents to the police. “The government and rail industry are taking this extremely seriously, with a £63m increase in British Transport Police funding by 2028-29, which will see over 200 additional officers recruited.” New measures called railway behaviour notices were introduced in June 2026, strengthening the railway’s ability to exclude repeat offenders from stations. BTP said they had been encouraging greater reporting of all types of assault by staff and passengers, including record use of the 61016 discreet text-to-report number, which partly explained the growing numbers. Nonetheless, the BTP assistant chief constable said: “These figures are a stark reminder of the violence and abuse rail workers face simply for doing their jobs. We will never tolerate violence or abuse directed at passengers or staff on the railway, and anyone committing these crimes can expect a robust response from us. “We remain committed to driving down these offences and ensuring the network is safe for everyone.” skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Business Today Get set for the working day – we'll point you to all the business news and analysis you need every morning after newsletter promotion The chief inspector of railways, the ORR’s Richard Hines, said the increase in reported assaults was concerning, adding: “No one on the railway should be subjected to violence, threats or abuse.” He said the ORR had set out guidance for employers on the risks, effective controls and encouraging staff to report incidents. View image in fullscreen The RMT is calling for increased rail staffing, including an end to lone working, and stronger legal protections for public transport workers. Photograph: Murdo MacLeod/The Guardian A spokesperson for Network Rail and train operators said: “Violence, abuse and intimidation directed at passengers or staff are completely unacceptable. The rail industry works closely with British Transport Police to investigate incidents, support victims and bring offenders to justice.” They said the numbers also reflected greater intelligence sharing, improved reporting processes, and more CCTV and body-worn cameras for frontline staff. The ORR report noted that the headline numbers of reported assaults can include multiple counts in a single incident, for example for both harassment and common assault, while workforce assaults are now recorded even if no physical injury occurs. On the London Underground, where there is single counting, the number of assaults on the workforce fell slightly last year. The chief executive of the Rail Safety and Standards Board, Mark Phillips, said the rail industry was taking action to better protect staff, but the figures “underline the need for a change in public behaviour and greater respect for the people who keep the railway running safely every day”. Reports in recent years have highlighted that women and girls were at particular risk , while the growing number of assaults year on year since the pandemic has coincided with pressure on British Transport Police numbers. The abuse and intimidation faced by frontline staff on the railways has also been seen in sectors including retail and in the NHS. The British Retail Consortium warned over “endemic” violence towards shop workers earlier this year, while the number of reports of violence against NHS staff by patients surpassed 100,000 in 2025 . https://www.eurasiareview.com/15092026-m.text: South China Sea Territorial Claims: Credit: VOA Analysis 1 East Asia Pacific Social Issues September 15, 2026 September 15, 2026 Dr. Rajaram Panda 0 Comments By Dr. Rajaram Panda Key Takeaways: At Seoul Defense Dialogue 2026, Philippine Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro restated UNCLOS and the 2016 Hague ruling against China’s nine-dash line, and held talks with South Korea and USFK on a closer defense partnership. A note from a Chinese military attaché called that award void. Teodoro rejected it as coercion and disrespect to the host; Beijing accused him of grandstanding. The author says Chinese pressure, not a U.S. plot, is what pulls Manila toward Washington, Tokyo, Canberra, and Seoul. Sea confrontations continue. The South China Sea issue, often seen as a major flashpoint in the Indo-Pacific region because of contesting claims by some countries to this global common, emerged as a hot topic of discussion at the Seoul Defence Dialogue 2026 held on 7-9 September. Philippines which has a running spat with China and took the matter to the International Court of Arbitration at The Hague and obtained a verdict in its favour in 2016 was represented by Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr, Secretary of National Defense. He was joined by senior defence officials, policy makers, and security experts from all over the globe in discussions on the evolving regional and global security environment. The Seoul Defense Dialogue is an annual multilateral security forum hosted by South Korea’s Defense Ministry since 2012 to promote peace on the Korean Peninsula and regional security cooperation. It was elevated to a ministerial-level forum in 2023. The three-day event, in its 15th year, brought together about 1,000 officials and experts from 67 countries and international organizations, including the defense ministers of the Czech Republic, Papua New Guinea, the Philippines and Uganda. In the first plenary session titled, “Collaborative Architecture for International Stability,” Secretary Teodoro reaffirmed the Philippines’ commitment to international law and a rules-based international order, including adherence to United National Laws of the Sea (UNCLOS) of 1982 and the 2016 South China Sea Arbitral Award. The Court of Arbitration in its award in 2016 denied most of China’s claims in the South China Sea as “illegal, null and void”. He emphasized the value of cooperation among partners in advancing peace, stability, and security, and underscored the need for an international security architecture that places human security at its core. Teodoro held bilateral meetings on the sidelines of the Dialogue with Republic of Korea Minister of National Defense Ahn Gyu-back and United Nations Command/United States Forces Korea Commander Gen. Xavier Brunson, among other engagements. Discussions focused on further strengthening the Philippines–ROK Strategic Partnership, particularly in defense cooperation, modernization, military exchanges, interoperability, emerging security domains, and regional security. The handout released by the Philippine Embassy in Seoul, mentioned that senior Philippine defense officials also took part in bilateral engagements and in the SDD Space Security and Cyber Working Groups. Both Philippines and South Korea resolved to deepen the defence and security pillars of the Strategic Partnership through sustained dialogue, practical cooperation, and closer exchanges. What emerged as outstanding and caught everyone’s eyes was that the forum became a stage for Teodoro to sharply criticise China over the South China Sea, though it was originally intended to promote dialogue and security cooperation among officials and experts from dozens of countries. While speaking at the first plenary session focusing on ways to build a more stable international over amid growing geopolitical tensions, Teodoro turned to South China Sea dispute, accusing some countries of using hostility and unchecked power at the expense of smaller states and stressing the need to uphold international law, including the UNCLOS. Teodoro was categorical saying that the Philippines would not sacrifice its territory or sovereignty and would continue to resist actions that violated international law, in remarks widely seen as directed at China. As he continued his criticism, he was handed a note from someone in the audience. Briefly looking at it, he realised the note was from China. As it transpired the note said that the “so-called arbitral award is illegal, null and void.” Replying “that is your claim” Teodoro, the note appeared to refer to a 2016 arbitration ruling issued in a case brought by the Philippines under UNCLOS. The tribunal rejected China’s claim to historic rights over much of the South China Sea under its “nine-dash line.” Then Teodoro went ballistic, saying that “Have a little bit of decency, have a little bit of shame”. He noted that the note represented disrespect both for the forum and international law. It may be noted that Chinese representatives took part in the Forum but were not featured as panelists or speakers. Over a decade has passed since the arbitral ruling but China’s position remains the same. It has refused to recognize the ruling and continues to assert claims over large parts of the waters, bringing Chinese and Philippine vessels into repeated confrontations in areas claimed by Manila. Teodoro was categorical saying that if the note represented China’s position, it amounted to “throwing UNCLOS on the floor and trampling on it.” He also criticized what he described as a lack of basic courtesy toward South Korea as the host of the forum. Since no senior Chinese government official attended the event, it remained unclear if the note came from a Chinese government or delegation official. Beijing sees that Philippines is acting as a US proxy and provoking China. That is a question of perception how nations see each other based on issues that go beyond bilateral issues. There is no denying the fact that China’s aggressive stances are pulling other nations that respect global rules to come together and see common ground. This deterrence mechanism is the propelling factor for countries such as the US, Japan, Australia, South Korea, Taiwan and the Philippines to see common ground to address the common challenges confronting them. Teodoro went further and observed that China’s handwritten memo on arbitration ruling as “coercion and bullying”. Undeterred, Beijing accused Philippine officials of “grandstanding and lying” after Teodoro read out the note on the South China Sea and described as “coercion, bullying and aggression”. Chinese foreign ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning urged Philippines to stop this grandstanding and lying, and to protect China-Philippine relations qnd peace and stability in the South China Sea. It remained a mystery for a while about the source of the note given to Teodoro but it soon transpired that the note came from a military attaché at the Chinese embassy in Seoul, who passed it to a forum staff member and asked that it be given to Teodoro. Teodoro saw the move as impolite to their South Korean hosts, disrespecting the organiser of the forum and lacked civility, besides disrespecting international law. The note episode came amid heightened tension over the disputed waters in the South China Sea, where confrontations – and sometimes clashes – between coastguard and naval vessels from China and the Philippines have prompted concern of a military escalation that could draw in the United States, a treaty ally of the Philippines. Philippines accuses China of firing water cannon at its vessels frequently and violating its fishing rights. In June, in a rare move targeting a sitting senior foreign official, Beijing announced sanctions on Teodoro for what Beijing said were erroneous remarks against China that undermined China’s legitimate interests and damaged bilateral relations. As commented succinctly by an analyst in an earlier post in the Eurasiareview, the Seoul Defence Dialogue Forum became more than a conventional defence and security forum, exposing the widening strategic contest over the “rules, norms, and balance of power” in the Indo-Pacific. The narrative of the argument, accusations and counter accusations seemed to have changed, portraying China as the restrained party and Philippines is the provocateur being encouraged by external power to confront China. Only the naives would buy such argument as Beijing’s assertiveness and aggressive behaviour on a host of bilateral and regional issues are for everyone to see. Beijing’s narrative that Philippines is drawn into a security cooperation with the US, Japan, Australia, South Korea and other partner countries and be a part of its containment strategy is flawed as Beijing’s aggressive posture on regional issues has led to a strategic reaction by regional states so that regional equilibrium is not unduly altered.
